html:
Performers
Detroit Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Paul Paray (conductor) Documented

Named on the original Mercury label and in the transfer metadata. Individual orchestra players are not identified.

[1] [2]
Work version
Original orchestral scoring Documented

The LP identifies the orchestral work. The precise edition, editorial alterations and part materials used by Paray are not established; no La Mer brass variant is used as a timing anchor.

[1] [5]
Recorded
1955-12-03/1955-12-04 Inferred, not documented

The later label documentation groups the Debussy titles with 1955 and 1959 dates. Faune is attributed to the December 1955 sessions; this is not a day-level identification of the particular take. The mono LP was issued in 1956.

[4]
Place
Old Orchestra Hall, Detroit, Michigan, United States Documented

The label names the recording venue; the LP issue date and modern digitisation date are distinct.

[4]
Label
Mercury Living Presence Documented

Original mono LP imprint, not the label of a later CD reissue.

[2] [1]
Catalogue
MG 50101 Documented

The transferred US mono LP is catalogued by Internet Archive as a 1956 release.

[2] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1, band 4 Documented

Side and band follow the label and segmented filenames. No runout matrix, stamper, session take or original tape number has been established.

[2] [3]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP transfer Documented

The operator account is transcribed as an account identifier, not expanded into an unverified personal or mastering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
2020-11-21 Documented

Derived directly from the item’s ripping_date field, 20201121083807. The 2020-10-21 scan date is a separate event.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → RDL EZ-PH1 → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 access derivative. Documented

The item documents the playback and digitisation chain. Equalisation settings, pitch correction, noise reduction and further restoration are not established.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Underlying Debussy composition is out of copyright under ordinary life-plus-70 terms; the original published score is historical. Inferred, not documented

Debussy died in 1918. This is a term assessment of the composition, not a blanket clearance for unidentified modern editions or every jurisdiction.

[6] [5]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: lawful commercial publication in 1956, before 1963. Documented

The 1956 Mercury mono LP publication predates 1963; under the programme’s rule its former 50-year phonogram term expired before the 2013 extension. First lawful publication anywhere is the relevant event; a US LP release can supply that date. US recording status is not established. This is not a Creative Commons licence or worldwide clearance.

[1] [2] [7]

Claude Debussy, Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune; Detroit Symphony Orchestra, Paul Paray. Mercury MG 50101 (mono, 1956); Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established.
